Companion image: out/probe_map.jpg (numbered probe points on the component-side photo). Companion list: research/BEEP_LIST_V3.md — its top 5 items (suspected solder bridge, R18/LK4 paradox, SCR1 map, pot paths, relay-rail chain) carry the highest information-per-beep on the board; do them alongside Session A. Sequence matters: everything in Session A is safe (board unpowered, meter only) and several powered tests are only interpretable after A.

Safety (read once, follow always)

This board is line-referenced EVERYWHERE, including all "5 V" logic points — the supply is transformerless and (pending DP1) the logic rail is tied to NEUTRAL, which is still a current-carrying line conductor. Powered work: isolation transformer AND a fused, current-limited feed; one-hand rule; pre-wired insulated fixtures only; nothing touched while energized; no grounded scope (battery DMM / diff probe only). Before ANY handling after power-down: discharge probe 17 (the red 2.2 µF/400 V cap) through ~1 kΩ, then the electrolytics.

Session A — unpowered beeps (~30 min, meter only)

COM = probe 2 (IC1 pin 20, VSS) unless stated. "≈0 Ω" means < a few Ω.

# Test (probe numbers) Expect if design-notes model right Settles
A1 ORIENTATION GATE: pin 6 (6) ↔ COM ≈0 Ω (VPP strapped to VSS) Q8. If A1 fails, STOP — pin numbering is flipped; tell Claude before anything else
A2 pin 1 (1) ↔ P5 spade ≈0 Ω (already beeped once) M003 re-check
A3 P5 ↔ P6 spades OPEN QUESTION — the v3 optical netlist keeps P5 and P6 SEPARATE; the DP1 reference-design model predicted them merged. Either result is informative — record it DP1 arbiter
A3b falsifiers: P5 ↔ P7, P6 ↔ P7, IC1.1 ↔ P6 P5↔P7 NO beep; P6↔P7 NO beep; IC1.1↔P6 beep rules out rival line-referenced topology
A4 ZD2 (9): K ↔ P6, A ↔ COM both ≈0 Ω (shunt across rails) DP2
A5 25 V cans: + ↔ P6, − ↔ COM ≈0 Ω each DP3
A6 C10, C11 ↔ RES1 legs (11) and pins 3/4 (4)(5) each cap to one leg/pin DP4, Q5
A7 pin 7 (3) ↔ nearby 10 nF cap; pin 7 ↔ R → P6 RC on reset DP5
A8 IC3 (8) LED: diode test pins 1–2 ~1.0–1.2 V one way 4N35 front end
A9 IC3 pins 4/5 ↔ P8 chain / P13 chain continuity into SEQ path DP6
A10 T1 gate (14) → pins 16–19 (7), RESISTANCE mode; same for T2 (15) a few hundred Ω–few kΩ via gate resistor (won't beep) DP7
A11 adjacent-pin beeps pins 16↔17↔18↔19↔20 NO beeps between them mask-fusion doubt (verification finding)
A12 P10 ↔ P11 spades either outcome informative — no netlist prediction (an earlier common-RET claim was withdrawn as a CV artifact) Q4 RET topology
A13 P10 ↔ P6 ≈0 Ω or a small R DP8 (RET returns to neutral?)
A14 LK2's two ends (the link just below pin 20) beep closes the flagged ambiguous link
A15 P2 ↔ its diode pad; P3 ↔ its diode pad (D17/18/19 cluster) beep each binds the runs CV lost to glare
A16 R32 (12) leads → D11/D12 node and coil pad, RESISTANCE mode ~4.7 kΩ through R32; coil side reads coil's 6.4 kΩ DP10
A17 relay coil low side (13) → TO-92s, DIODE mode both polarities junction signature to one TR's collector DP10
A18 pin 5 (NMI) ↔ COM and ↔ P6, RESISTANCE mode strap (≈0) or resistor network; a high-R line divider will read open — that case resolves only powered DP11
A19 flex test: press near P5-chain link pads + P10/P11 while beeping A2/A12 no dropouts fault-tree #4
A20 visual: P10/P11 solder joints under magnification reflow if cracked/cold rework evidence
A22 read RES1's printed frequency marking (raking light) 4 MHz vs 8 MHz clock-spec margin: 8 MHz needs VDD>=4.5V — a sagging dropper rail is out of spec (MCU_USAGE_NOTES)
A21 P14 and P15 → IC1 pins 8–15 sweep (also to R14/R15/R16/R17 ends) each pot reaches ONE MCU input via a series R the XLO-request input path — the fault's front door (netlist could not follow it under the parts)

Interpretation shortcuts: - A3 beep → P5≡P6≡VDD as one NODE (DP1 model confirmed; several v3 nets merge); A3 open → the v3 optical netlist stands (PB0/pin-15 straps to NEUT, VDD is its own node). The wider neutral-referenced supply MODEL (rectifier scheme, relay-rail split, drive scheme) stays hypothesis until A4-A18 and the powered checks land. A4/A5/A7/A13/A16-A18 are TOPOLOGY TESTS (they map the board), not pass/fail health checks — record whatever they show. If A3b shows P5↔P7 beeping instead, the supply is line-referenced: the bench plan still works but tell Claude first (several expectations flip). - A11 beeps anywhere → tell Claude; the IC1 pin-16–20 nets need re-cutting (model imposed those separations). - A15 fails → the D17-cluster runs are broken copper (crack), itself a candidate fault.

Session B — powered bench (only after A; safety block above)

Setup: isolation + current-limited 120 V to P7 (LINE) / P6 (NEUT). Loads: real XLO solenoid or 1.7 kΩ/10 W across P9→P10 (and P12→P11 for channel 2). Pot rig: 10 kΩ pot pre-wired P5→P14 (+ its switch line per the service-manual harness diagram), insulated, hands-off.

# Test Healthy Sick → meaning
B1 VDD–VSS (probes 1↔2), idle ~5 V steady; AC range < ~0.3 V (note: DMM AC on 120 Hz sawtooth reads approximately — treat >1 V as definitely sick, <0.3 V as probably fine) low/collapsing → PSU/load-path fault CLASS
B2 pin 7 (3) vs VSS ≈VDD steady sawtooth/cycling → brown-out or reset RC (FMEA #2)
B3 pins 3/4 (4)(5) DC vs VSS mid-rail-ish (osc running) stuck at rail → resonator dead (and OSG not enabled)
B4 B1 again while relay pulls in + solenoid load ≤10 % sag collapse → PSU/load-path fault CLASS confirmed — then branch: SERIES dropper C12 (B4a: bridge C12 with a known-good X2 of the same value, retest — NOT C7, which the netlist shows as the LINE↔NEUT filter), reservoir ESR (B4b: parallel a good electrolytic briefly, retest), zener/rectifier (B4c: diode-test D11/D12, powered zener voltage), relay-rail/R32/driver, or a cracked joint moving under relay clunk
B5 48 V rail across relay coil when commanded ~48 V absent → R32 branch / driver TR / MCU never commands
B6 functional: turn pot rig through range, assert request relay clicks, solenoid clunks, drive appears on P9–P10 (half-wave: expect ~50–85 V depending on DMM coupling — value is a consistency check, not a topology proof), pins 16–19 switching (v3 could not optically bind pins 16/17 — whatever you record here completes that map) no PA activity w/ good B1–B3 → request path OR pot/stimulus wiring OR zero-cross sense OR firmware in fault-latch — vary one at a time; PA switches but no solenoid → triac/steering/SCR kicker
B7 relay contact drop P7↔P4 under load < 0.2 V high → burned contacts
B8 across SCR1 (16) / red cap (17) at command moment discharge event at pull-in (a DMM may miss the ms-scale pulse — absence on a DMM is NOT proof; needs min/max capture or scope-with-diff-probe) repeatable absence with proper capture → kicker path suspect

False-pass/false-fail (from red-team): a bench PASS with an unrealistic load can still hide an in-range fault (harness parasitics, heat); a FAIL only counts if the stimulus wiring truly replicates one XLO position. When in doubt, bring the range's actual solenoid + pot to the bench.

Decision tree after B

  • B1/B4 sick → replace C12 (same value, X2 safety class) + both 25 V cans (105 °C low-ESR) + re-test → expected total parts <$10. This is FMEA #1/#2.
  • B1–B3 healthy, B6 dead at request → Session A's request-path parts (4N35, D17–D20, their Rs) and the pot/harness on the range side.
  • B5 dead with MCU alive → R32 branch / driver TR / relay.
  • Everything healthy on bench → fault is range-side (pots, harness, connectors) or thermal-only: re-test warm (hairdryer on the board, NOT powered handling).

Recording results

Append to measurements.yaml like:

- id: M012
  type: continuity
  nodes: [P5, P6]
  beeps: true
  date: 2026-07-26
  note: DP1 neutral-referenced supply CONFIRMED

(ids increment; nodes use P1..P15, IC1.1..IC1.20, refdes.pin). Then tell Claude — the pipeline ingests these as ground truth, upgrades net confidences, and the schematic regenerates.

B9 — reset-cause classifier (pin 7), from the ST62T20C datasheet

With the board powered in the fault state, measure IC1 pin 7 (/RESET) vs pin 20 (VSS): static low = LVD/brown-out holding the MCU in reset (go to the PSU branch, B1/B4); repeating 0.4–25 ms sawtooth (scope, or a DMM reading a suspicious mid-level average) = watchdog reset loop (crash loop: oscillator, rail dips, or corrupted OTP); solid high = the MCU believes it is running — the fault is in inputs (pots! ADC needs <=10k source impedance), outputs, or firmware-level refusal (sanity-stop). This single measurement splits the fault tree in three.
